facts.statement: K3 SoC integrates 8 X100 general-purpose cores and 8 A100 AI cores (2 A100 clusters, 60 TOPS aggregate AI compute) using RISC-V homogeneous fusion: scalar (standard ISA), vector (RVV 1.0) and matrix (IME extension) compute share one RISC-V programming model, and standard Linux threads drive AI computation without a heterogeneous scheduler or driver management.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/432da714bd719f3506e3fb28b39f1f35fa1a8f54702382d66e010ec92acb30f6/root_overview.md.search.txt:12-14; docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/83ddde6d173d633a2b89bad966f7ec23ae7ab4699185cf85989521a79c03d066/concept.md.search.txt:11-22 (4.1.1); docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/9564d4ba5ed9a64d71c0c7e5bf0c8f7d74ed717fd0aa71265328f8c1eaea8c91/K3_architecture_preview.pdf.search.txt:181-183

facts.statement: A100 execution resources (Preview 2026-01-29 description, to be reconciled with production hardware at board porting): each of the 2 A100 clusters comprises 4 scalar cores, 2 vector cores, 2 local-memory banks and a shared L2; the Tensor Core (IME-2.0, 1024/2048-bit datapath) is shared by two compute cores and accepts one MMA instruction per cycle from each; a per-core private IME-1.0 unit (256/512-bit, INT8xINT8->INT32 small MAC) also exists; each core has an independent 512-bit load channel and the front end dual-issues one 512-bit load plus one MMA per cycle.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/9564d4ba5ed9a64d71c0c7e5bf0c8f7d74ed717fd0aa71265328f8c1eaea8c91/K3_architecture_preview.pdf.search.txt:680-685,717-745 (3.2/3.2.2)

facts.statement: Execution-model policy for this compiler: parallelize one operator across native workers and vectorize within each worker; work may be repartitioned from the source grid when semantics permit; a persistent worker pool receives native work ranges and threads/workspaces are reused across calls; cross-worker dependencies use explicit stages, synchronization and merges; coverage, tails, ownership, visibility and repeated execution must be validated at 1/2/4/8 workers, and representative multi-worker cases must distribute useful work.
facts.source: chip.md#3-execution-model (POLICY, lines 63-70)

facts.statement: Measured scheduling model under the declared QEMU endpoint: a persistent pthread pool executes work ranges with distinct guest tids at 1/2/4/8 threads (full 32771-item coverage, one pool initialization, warmup run included) - the scheduling unit is the OS-scheduled Linux thread; a worker count of one is the single-thread serial configuration. QEMU guest threads are not physical A100 cores (assumption A001).
facts.source: probe: TOOLCHAIN_PROBES.json threads rows (persistent_pool_two_stages, qemu-functional, passed=true at 1/2/4/8); docs/compiler-agent/ENVIRONMENT.md Multi-worker execution/observation

facts.statement: Vendor-stack scheduling reference (not this project's codegen contract): the official X100 runtime dispatches tile-level compute tasks onto A100-cluster thread groups - one A100 cluster maps to a group of four A100 Linux threads, two clusters form two groups totalling eight A100 Linux threads, dispatched least-loaded; official inference examples assign AI core IDs 8-15 explicitly (SPACEMIT_PERFER_CORE_ID=8,9,10,11 / 12,13,14,15) and K3 provides 8 AI cores supporting up to 8-thread inference. These are documented examples; the actual allowed core set must be probed on the board.

facts.statement: Board address spaces (K3 main CPU domain map): RISCV TCM 64MB at 0x0000_0000; DDR DRAM 64GB at 0x1_0000_0000; 128KB boot-ROM; 512KB SRAM shared by Main CPU and Real CPU domains; hardware Spinlock (32 units, 1KB window) at 0xCAC9_1C00; Mailbox0-6; AIDMA_0-7, DMA350_0-1 and HSDMA controllers. RCPU domain additionally maps its own SRAM view.

facts.statement: A100 per-cluster memory hierarchy: 32KB L1 I-cache and 32KB L1 D-cache per core; 1MB L2 cache per cluster; 1.5MB scratchpad per cluster; L1 D-cache supports MESI and L2 supports MOESI coherence. The L2 and the 1.5MB scratchpad are cluster-shared resources, not per-thread private capacity.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/ff2340c355516e190769949abbfe57d2121efbe72326b5fc65b166f6cd55d90d/08_cpu.md.search.txt:54-59 (8.2.2); docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/69a7cd5b8836085506f53f1b02ad8aa624790eb23ca573ca584e226ee1246358/k3_ds.md.search.txt:147-153

facts.statement: Per-hart local storage: each A100 hart has a private vector register file of 32 vector registers x 128B = 4KB at VLEN=1024, which the architecture Preview describes as an effective 4KB ultra-fast local scratchpad for locality optimizations (e.g. holding a broadcast Scale vector or a FlashAttention accumulation in registers).
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/9564d4ba5ed9a64d71c0c7e5bf0c8f7d74ed717fd0aa71265328f8c1eaea8c91/K3_architecture_preview.pdf.search.txt:727-731 (3.2.1),1261-1267 (5.2.2)

facts.statement: The A100 dataflow design (Preview) uses software-managed local memory and decoupled access-execute operation - asynchronous DMA prefetch overlapping memory movement with computation; the K3 DMA controller is a 16-channel flow-through engine (memory-to-memory/peripheral, burst 8/16/32/64B, up to 8191 bytes per descriptor with chaining, 64-bit addressing above 4GB). The software interfaces for TCM/DMA allocation, completion, visibility and lifetime are not specified in the pack and remain unverified (assumption A00x).
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/9564d4ba5ed9a64d71c0c7e5bf0c8f7d74ed717fd0aa71265328f8c1eaea8c91/K3_architecture_preview.pdf.search.txt:666-672 (3.2 dataflow axes); docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/e3c328de09ccec8594134bfa2d29c635b7cc78578dde2cfe28de169983b9ecb7/dma.md.search.txt:7-42 (16.1.1-16.1.2)

facts.statement: A100 ISA baseline: fully compliant with the RISC-V RVA23* standard (RVA23U64 user + RVA23S64 supervisor) EXCLUDING the Hypervisor extension; SV39 virtual memory; 32 PMP entries; integrated PMU; ACLINT + APLIC interrupt controllers (AIA). Optional extensions listed: vector crypto zvkng/zvksg, plus zvbc, zfh, zbc, zvfh, zfbfmin, zvfbfmin, zvfbfwma, sdtri, svvptc, sspm, smepmp, smstateen, smcntrpmf. RVA23U64 makes V (vector) mandatory together with Zvfhmin/Zvbb/Zvkt.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/ff2340c355516e190769949abbfe57d2121efbe72326b5fc65b166f6cd55d90d/08_cpu.md.search.txt:53-76 (8.2.2 incl. facts.statement: A100 vector extension: RVV 1.0 with VLEN=1024; the Vector Unit is driven by two parallel vector pipelines performing instruction splitting, dependency handling and vector register-file reads/writes; operators are classified INT, FP, CRYPTO, FDV and IME-1.0 by instruction type and datapath; the register file provides 32 architectural vector registers v0-v31 of 128B each.

facts.statement: SpacemiT IME instruction set (Zvvm_spacemit profile, version 0.6 public release 2026-04-13): 46 custom AI instructions, all prefixed smt. (SMT vendor prefix); it reuses the 32 RVV vector registers for 2D matrix tiles with no dedicated matrix register file (no extra architectural state or context-switch overhead). The A100 core in K3 supports 13 sub-extensions: Xsmti4i32mm, Xsmti8i32mm, Xsmti8i32mm_slide, Xsmti4i32mm_42sp, Xsmti8i32mm_42sp, Xsmti4fp16mm_scl16f, Xsmti4bf16mm_scl16f, Xsmti8fp16mm_scl16f, Xsmti8bf16mm_scl16f, Xsmtfp16fp32mm, Xsmtbf16fp32mm, Xsmtfp16fp32mm_slide, Xsmtbf16fp32mm_slide; the toolchain names the A100 set collectively Xsmtvdotii. Chinese and English v0.6 editions in the pack agree.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:5-9,56,206-243 (1.6/1.7),2333-2339 (App. B); cross-checked with the Chinese edition docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/efb5d87ac66581c12a931698b95db2ae840a57110cf23e429142fca07662e189/ime_extension.md.search.txt:91-144

facts.statement: A100 IME tile shapes and implementation parameters (LMUL=1 tiles): INT4 x INT4 -> INT32 tile 8x32x8; INT8 x INT8 -> INT32 tile 8x16x8 (integer family: lambda=4, MUL_C=2, SEW=32); FP16/BF16 x FP16/BF16 -> FP32 tile 8x8x8 (MUL_C=2, SEW=32); 4:2 structured sparse: INT4 8x64x8, INT8 8x32x8; block-scaled integer (Int4/Int8 + FP16/BF16 scale -> FP16/BF16): lambda=8, MUL_C=1, SEW=16, tiles 8x32x8 (Int4) / 8x16x8 (Int8); sliding-window variants keep their base family tile. lambda is fixed per instruction family and NOT configurable via vtype; MUL_C = VLEN/(SEW x lambda^2).
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:274-317 (2.1.2),371-396 (2.5),2313-2329 (App. A)

facts.statement: IME operand and data-layout contract: vs1 holds tile A (row-major), vs2 holds tile B (column-major); B^T in the semantics C <- C + A x B^T is a geometric layout statement and does NOT require a software transpose of B; vd holds both the initial accumulator and the result with an implementation-defined result layout; Int4 inputs use packed nibble storage (element 2n in bits [3:0], 2n+1 in bits [7:4] of byte n); EEW=8/16 use standard linear vector element ordering; integer signedness variants (none/u/us/su) select signed/unsigned interpretation of A and B with the accumulator always signed.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:67-86 (1.4),144-155 (1.5),437-479 (2.7),529-538 (4.2)

facts.statement: Negative ISA facts - absent operations in the SpacemiT matrix extension: community Zvvm instructions vmmacc, vwmmacc, vfmmacc, vfqwmmacc and vf8wmmacc are NOT supported (functional equivalents: vqwmmacc->smt.vmadot* Int8, v8wmmacc->smt.vmadot* Int4, vfwmmacc->smt.vfwmadot, vfwimmacc->smt.vmadot.hp* Int8+scale, vfqwimmacc->smt.vmadot.hp* Int4+scale; vf8wimmacc e5m2 scale not supported); the Zvvmtls dedicated matrix load/store extension is NOT implemented (similar functionality via smt.vpack); mixed FP16/BF16 input formats within one instruction are NOT defined; the standard RVV vm mask bit is NOT used as a mask control for matrix multiplication instructions (no vector-mask semantics defined for this instruction class); Zvvm vtype.lambda / vtype.altfmt_A/B / vtype.altfmt CSR fields are not implemented (A100 uses MCPM instead).
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:329-346 (2.3),489-513 (Ch.3 differences table),1397-1404 (6.1.3)

facts.statement: IME illegal conditions (refusal/trap contract): LMUL != 1 in any IME instruction raises an illegal instruction exception (all other LMUL encodings reserved); when MUL_C=2 the destination vd must be even-numbered (vd and vd+1 form the group) and the destination group must not overlap vs1 or vs2; sliding-window instructions additionally require vs1 even-numbered; sparse instructions use v0/v1 as recovery masks with imm2 segment select; scale instructions use v0/v1 as scale parameter registers with imm3 group select; for smt.vfwmadot* the floating-point input format must match the MCPM.BF16 setting, else illegal.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:104-129 (1.5),329-352 (2.3),398-435 (2.6),670-675 (5.1.4),1424-1429 (6.1.5)

facts.statement: Register model: 32 general-purpose registers (RISC-V standard) plus 32 architectural vector registers v0-v31 at 128B each (VLEN=1024) per A100 hart; v0 serves the standard RVV mask-register role; the vector register file is per-core private; the IME reuses exactly these vector registers for matrix tiles with no additional architectural state, so matrix context switching carries no cost beyond ordinary RVV state.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/9564d4ba5ed9a64d71c0c7e5bf0c8f7d74ed717fd0aa71265328f8c1eaea8c91/K3_architecture_preview.pdf.search.txt:727-731,739-745 (3.2.1/3.2.2); docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:25-38 (1.1)

facts.statement: IME register budget and granularity: input matrices A and B each occupy a single vector register (LMUL=1 only; every other LMUL encoding reserved and illegal in IME instructions); the accumulator tile occupies MUL_C registers - MUL_C=2 for the integer and fp16/bf16-fp32 families (vd even-numbered, vd+vd+1 group) and MUL_C=1 for the block-scaled families (any vd); the destination group must not overlap vs1/vs2; MUL_C is fixed per Profile, not a dynamically configurable parameter; sparse paths additionally consume v0/v1 (recovery masks) and scale paths v0/v1 (scale parameters), so those paths have 30 generally usable vector registers.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:104-129 (1.5),254-269 (2.1.2 tables),319-369 (2.2-2.4),398-435 (2.6)

facts.statement: Register-budget failure modes: exceeding IME legality (LMUL!=1, odd vd where MUL_C=2, destination/source overlap, format inconsistent with MCPM.BF16, non-even vs1 in sliding-window) raises an illegal instruction exception at execution - these are hardware traps the compiler must prevent by construction (check before emission); by contrast, exceeding the 32x128B vector register budget has no architectural spill mechanism - spill/split decisions are compiler-owned, and the Preview notes heavy LMUL=4/8 use is prone to vector-register spills (with VLEN=1024, LMUL=1 already gives 1024-bit compute width, reducing spill likelihood).
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:110-113,670-675,1424-1429 (illegal conditions); docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/9564d4ba5ed9a64d71c0c7e5bf0c8f7d74ed717fd0aa71265328f8c1eaea8c91/K3_architecture_preview.pdf.search.txt:1275-1285 (5.2.2 spill note)

assumptions.statement: No physical A100 board is reachable from this environment; all target execution uses the pinned QEMU functional emulator, and QEMU guest threads do not establish physical A100 core identities, topology, affinity, cache behaviour or timing.
assumptions.why_needed: chip.md marks board topology and timing as UNKNOWN and declares board porting as a later step; the environment provides only the emulator endpoint, so board properties cannot be probed here.
assumptions.validation_method: On-board discovery and probes during the porting step; until then no topology, affinity or timing conclusion may be drawn from QEMU runs.

assumptions.statement: The containerized no-Python execution round trip (a100_support/run-candidate-container.sh running a generated operator_exec inside image a100-qemu-functional:compiler-a100-experiment-001) has not been exercised end-to-end; only image presence and docker CLI usability were probed.
assumptions.why_needed: No compiler-generated operator executable exists yet, so the candidate container path cannot be exercised with a real artifact during environment analysis.
assumptions.validation_method: Run a100_support/run-candidate-container.sh with the first generated operator executable and record the executed result.

assumptions.statement: Standard RISC-V unprivileged semantics hold for the non-universal integer cases (wrap-around signed overflow, division/remainder by zero defined not trapping, shift amounts masked to the operand width) and standard RVV 1.0 FP semantics (frm-controlled rounding) via RVA23 compliance; the pack states RVA23* compliance but does not restate these behaviours.
assumptions.why_needed: The compiler's arithmetic lowering and basic-optimization legality conditions depend on integer overflow/div/shift semantics; the target documents only profile compliance.
assumptions.validation_method: Bounded probe under the declared QEMU endpoint (div-by-zero, overwide shift, wrap cases, an frm rounding check) and re-verification on the board at porting; until then treat as RISC-V-standard.

assumptions.statement: Vector and scalar memory operands are naturally aligned; the compiler emits aligned accesses with masked tails and does not rely on misaligned access support. The pack does not state misaligned or out-of-range access behaviour for A100.
assumptions.why_needed: Predicated/tail lowering and wide-access grouping legality depend on the alignment contract.
assumptions.validation_method: Bounded misaligned-access probe under the declared QEMU endpoint (expect exception or defined behaviour, recorded either way); on-board check at porting; keep aligned-plus-mask codegen until verified.

assumptions.statement: The FMA contraction/rounding detail of smt.vfwmadot (single-rounding fused versus two-rounding widen-then-multiply-add) is not specified by the IME v0.6 document; no exactness claim may rely on it. Floating outputs are compared within each case's declared tolerance, so either behaviour is within policy.
assumptions.why_needed: The spec gives program-visible semantics as fp32 accumulate but not the rounding-point contract.
assumptions.validation_method: If a case ever demands it, differential comparison of the executed instruction result against an independent fp32 reference at the used shapes; otherwise treat as tolerance-covered.

assumptions.statement: The formal memory model between A100 harts is assumed RVWMO (implied by RVA23 profile compliance) with per-level cache coherence as documented (MESI L1 D, MOESI L2 per cluster); the pack does not state the cross-cluster ordering contract. Generated cross-worker communication therefore uses explicit pthread/atomic synchronization and does not assume timing-based visibility.
assumptions.why_needed: Cross-worker merge correctness and any future reordering optimization depend on the visibility rule; only per-cache coherence protocols are documented.
assumptions.validation_method: On-board memory-ordering probes during porting (write-visibility across clusters with and without fences); under the pinned QEMU the guest is a single coherent address space so the assumption is untested there.

assumptions.statement: TCM, DMA and hardware-spinlock software interfaces (allocation, completion, visibility, lifetime) are unverified, and under the pinned QEMU endpoint these MMIO regions are not part of the userspace execution path; no generated code may assume TCM/DMA availability or asynchronous reuse until the interfaces are verified.
assumptions.why_needed: The manuals document the hardware but not the software allocation/completion contracts; the Preview's async-DMA dataflow needs matching SDK sources and probes.
assumptions.validation_method: Match SDK sources and run on-board probes (spacemit-tcm-smi resource state, TCM allocation/DMA completion/visibility) before any use; the correctness path uses Linux userspace memory only.

assumptions.statement: The production pairing of the shared IME-2.0 matrix engines (Preview: shared by two compute cores) and the actual allowed A100 core set (official examples use core IDs 8-15) are unverified on hardware; QEMU guest threads establish neither. Resource evidence under QEMU records guest threads, work partition and dynamic instruction counts, never physical core identities.
assumptions.why_needed: Work placement and matrix-throughput reasoning depend on the real topology; the Preview is an architectural description that production hardware must confirm.
assumptions.validation_method: On-board discovery during the porting step (probe eligible cores, confirm engine pairing and usable storage); extend assumption A001.

A003 Standard RISC-V unprivileged semantics hold for the non-universal integer cases (wrap-around signed overflow, division/remainder by zero defined not trapping, shift amounts masked to the operand width) and standard RVV 1.0 FP semantics (frm-controlled rounding) via RVA23 compliance; the pack states RVA23* compliance but does not restate these behaviours.

A004 Vector and scalar memory operands are naturally aligned; the compiler emits aligned accesses with masked tails and does not rely on misaligned access support. The pack does not state misaligned or out-of-range access behaviour for A100.

A005 The FMA contraction/rounding detail of smt.vfwmadot (single-rounding fused versus two-rounding widen-then-multiply-add) is not specified by the IME v0.6 document; no exactness claim may rely on it. Floating outputs are compared within each case's declared tolerance, so either behaviour is within policy.

A006 The formal memory model between A100 harts is assumed RVWMO (implied by RVA23 profile compliance) with per-level cache coherence as documented (MESI L1 D, MOESI L2 per cluster); the pack does not state the cross-cluster ordering contract. Generated cross-worker communication therefore uses explicit pthread/atomic synchronization and does not assume timing-based visibility.

A007 TCM, DMA and hardware-spinlock software interfaces (allocation, completion, visibility, lifetime) are unverified, and under the pinned QEMU endpoint these MMIO regions are not part of the userspace execution path; no generated code may assume TCM/DMA availability or asynchronous reuse until the interfaces are verified.

A008 The production pairing of the shared IME-2.0 matrix engines (Preview: shared by two compute cores) and the actual allowed A100 core set (official examples use core IDs 8-15) are unverified on hardware; QEMU guest threads establish neither. Resource evidence under QEMU records guest threads, work partition and dynamic instruction counts, never physical core identities.

Execute through the a100_support native device protocol (a factory shim) under QEMU and compare against the case's expected outputs with its declared comparison policy.

Implement in TIR and lowering: if/else with explicit join parameters for carried values (a source variable re-bound on one path must not merge with its earlier binding); tl.range (step; num_stages, loop_unroll_factor, disallow_acc_multi_buffer, flatten, warp_specialize, disable_licm classified ignorable-with-reason or honored); tl.static_range unrolling; while loops; program_id multi-axis decomposition; tl.num_programs from runtime grid extents; persistent grid-stride loops; if_pid patterns. Implement a100c/frontend/gridmodel.py: the provenance-tracking case-layer interpreter that extracts the grid expression for every corpus grid form (multi-axis tuples, cdiv products, lambda-meta form, shape-derived locals), proves every grid input equal to a bundle-visible quantity (scalar argument or view extent), emits the native grid-evaluation routine, and self-checks equality against the compiling case's concrete grid; operators whose grid inputs cannot be tied to bundle-visible quantities are refused with a located diagnostic (never baked), and the refusal count is reportable.

T009 Reductions, scans and cross-worker merge semantics. Implement: reduction operations (tl.sum, tl.max, tl.min, tl.argmax, tl.argmin with return_indices and return_indices_tie_break_left, tl.xor_sum, tl.reduce_or, tl.softmax, tl.cumsum, tl.cumprod scans, tl.histogram, tl.sort, tl.topk) with axis selection, keep_dims, per-operation-and-dtype identity elements (signedness-correct), empty-extent behaviour and declared index tie-breaking; intra-program RVV reductions; cross-worker two-phase splits (a100c/plan/stages.py: partial results to owned workspace regions, a stage barrier establishing visibility, a merge step combining partials under the source's own semantics — floating accumulation order preserved within the declared tolerance, exact for integer/index/boolean); persistent reductions looping chunks inside one program; split-K style reduction feeds for dot. Implement tools/check_stage_barriers.py: a two-phase multi-worker case is correct with the declared barrier; --witness removes the barrier in a scratch build and must fail (proving the synchronization test can fail).

T010 IME matrix slice with real instruction execution, before matrix breadth. Implement a100c/plan/tiles.py and a100c/lower/matrix.py: tl.dot lowering to the applicable IME families on the input path (F037) — INT8 8x16x8 -> INT32 via smt.vmadot with the u/us/su signedness variants (integer accumulation in 32-bit modular arithmetic, signed accumulator, F051) and FP16 8x8x8 -> FP32 via smt.vfwmadot (FP32 accumulation, F051); tile mapping with vs1 = A tile row-major and vs2 = B tile column-major (the geometric layout statement; no software transpose when the memory layout provides columns, otherwise packing via RVV loads or the smt.vpack family, F031/F035); K-loop accumulator chaining through the acc parameter; M/N/K tails via compiler-written zero-padded staging tiles (never reading out-of-range memory to construct a nominally neutral term) and masked M/N stores, with the ordinary RVV FMA path as a legal alternative for small or ragged tails; register grouping constraints (MUL_C=2: vd even-numbered, vd+vd+1 the group, destination group never overlapping vs1/vs2, F033/F040) enforced by the MIR verifier and honored by the allocator; implicit control state handled per the specification (MCPM.BF16 selects the 16-bit operand format and is not userspace-accessible under the pinned QEMU, so only FP16 operands reach IME floating tiles, F011/F034; the standard vm mask is not a matrix mask control and no vtype.lambda/altfmt fields exist, F032). BF16 tl.dot lowers to the vector FP32 path with the emulator gap recorded (F010/F034: BF16 IME execution is not claimable; never infer it from FP16 success). int4/sparse/scale source-level forms are outside the declared surface and refused. Execute one INT8 and one FP16 dot case under QEMU with the instruction-count plugin (a100_support/probes/instruction_counts.c, F008/F048): positive counted smt.vmadot / smt.vfwmadot executions bound to the same run, case and artifact.

T011 Memory access breadth and atomics. Implement: make_block_ptr / advance / load / store with boundary_check and padding_option; cache_modifier and eviction_policy classified ignorable-with-reason (performance-only) and volatile honored; tl.multiple_of / tl.max_contiguous hints feeding contiguity/alignment proofs for wide-access selection (unproven accesses keep masked or scalar forms); tl.gather; atomics (tl.atomic_add, max, min, xchg, and, or, xor, cas) with sem/scope parameters mapped to the declared RVWMO model with explicit fences — a masked atomic performs no access at disabled positions and keeps its signedness; tl.debug_barrier as intra-program ordering; pointer_table_relocations consumption (the grouped_gemm pattern: device addresses inside int64/uint64 buffers, patched by the bundle reader); tl.interleave. Scalar/integer paths: int64/bool/unsigned logic and index arithmetic with the declared wrap/shift/division semantics (A003).

T012 Layout, shape and dtype-conversion breadth. Implement: reshape (can_reorder classified), trans / permute (dims), join / split, cat, expand_dims / unsqueeze, squeeze, broadcast_to / broadcast, ravel, view (bit-level reinterpretation), flip, tl.swizzle2d (declared with 0 corpus calls: implement or declare-unsupported with a refusal witness), to_tensor / tensor; value-level dtype introspection folding. Implement the full conversion matrix over the corpus dtype pairs (bfloat16, bool, float16, float32, int16, int32, int64, int8, uint variants) with value conversion and bit-level reinterpretation as distinct constructs — an identity fold removes a conversion only when the types are value-identical, never when they merely print the same width; bf16 pointer duality handled for both staging forms (host float32-cast and host uint16-bitview, reading back symmetrically); fp16/bf16 compute lanes may use FP32 with one final rounding inside the declared tolerance (fp16 1e-2, bf16 2e-2; fp32 stays IEEE), as a declared numeric decision with a per-pass switch.

T013 Special math functions and bit-exact RNG. Implement: exp, exp2, log, log2, sqrt, sqrt_rn, rsqrt, sigmoid, erf, sin, cos, floor, ceil, clamp, pow, fma, div_rn, abs, maximum / minimum with propagate_nan, and the remaining declared math forms, with per-dtype accuracy inside each case's declared tolerance (fp32 IEEE; fp16/bf16 via FP32 lanes under the declared single-rounding policy); scalar constexpr math folded at specialization.
